messages:
jordan.sales: Quick sync — ACME wants to kick off the POC but procurement flagged a 20% holdback on the first invoice pending successful onboarding. They also want the signer to be a delegated procurement agent (not the contract signee). Anyone seen this pattern?
jordan.sales: They attached a redline of our order form with a new clause: 'commencement contingent on completion of onboarding checklist and technical ramp within 30 days.' link: https://acme.example/po-draft.pdf
claudia.finance: Ack, saw it. Holdback is common for large customers. Need to confirm if we can accept 20% or negotiate to 10% — impacts revenue recognition. Can we get a milestone schedule?
lee.legal: Sharing initial read — holdback clause is negotiable but we need clear language around "onboarding checklist" and objective acceptance criteria. Also the signer delegation needs a letter-of-authority or PO with authorized rep details.
lee.legal: If their delegated signer signs the PO, we still need an MSA signatory on file for the contract. We should not change the MSA signature table.
jordan.sales: Good point. They want countersignature to be via DocuSign by the delegated agent — they claim procurement has authority.
sam.engineering: From POC side: onboarding checklist must include network allowlisting, test model endpoint, and a lead time for dedicated capacity spin-up (if they choose Dedicated). I can draft a checklist. Timeline: 2 business days for host setup + up to 10 days if dedicated GPUs requested.
claudia.finance: Can we accept 'commencement contingent' phrase? Revenue folks prefer "commencement = first successful test completion" with defined tests. Not an open-ended checklist.
lee.legal: Proposed language to counter: "Commencement shall occur upon completion of the mutually agreed onboarding checklist described in Exhibit A, which shall include objective test cases and timelines. If timelines are missed, parties will follow the escalation procedure in Section X." Keeps it concrete.
jordan.sales: Perfect. Also they redlined the DPA to require EU data residency plus a 90-day log retention extension. That may need Product/security input.
sam.engineering: EU residency is doable in hosted regions but for POC we can propose a temporary scoped exception with pseudonymized logs. For 90-day retention we need sign-off from security. @doc-bot can you attach the security checklist we use for residency questions?
doc-bot: Attached: /assets/templates/security-residency-checklist.md 
lee.legal: On signer mapping, request a PO-level authorization letter or a signed delegated authority appendix. We can add a small clause: "Delegated Signer: Counterparty may designate an Authorized Procurement Representative for PO execution. Any such designation must be provided in writing and signed by a named Contract Signatory listed in the MSA."
claudia.finance: If they insist on 20% holdback, propose milestone payments: 50% net30, 30% on POC acceptance, 20% after 30-day stability period. Limits cash exposure.
jordan.sales: I'll propose that structure. Anyone object to proposing 10% holdback instead?
lee.legal: 10% is better for contract risk. If they push 20% take the milestone split Claudia suggested.
sam.engineering: I can create an onboarding checklist draft by EOD — will include test cases, required telemetry (pseudonymized), and gating criteria.
jordan.sales: Awesome. I'll update the order form with milestone schedule + delegate signer clause and push back on the open "commencement" wording. Will loop back with revised doc. :thumbsup:
claudia.finance: Thanks — ping me once you have the milestone amounts, I'll run through revenue treatment.
lee.legal: I'll prepare the legal redline for MSA + DPA changes and the delegated signer appendix.
jordan.sales: Thanks everyone. If ACME comes back with HSM/KMS requirements we may need Security advisory. Noted.
jordan.sales: tagging for follow-ups: @lee.legal @claudia.finance @sam.engineering
